items.title: Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-10-21
items.q: That was on Cronlade and St. Charles, a jitney dance.

ctx.x: Well, in the old days, did any of the guys support themselves by playing in brass bands only?

Well, no, they couldn't exactly, just in brass bands only. Some of them used to play at night, but they didn't, they didn't play in the brass bands. Because myself, I used to play in the music box every night. That was on Cronlade and St. Charles, a jitney dance. And I used to play it every night, but in the film, sometimes we'd have a film every day, putting it. And I was like, well, you see, I just started. But of course, at that time when I was playing, I played in the middle of the way, I couldn't drink. Like…
Well, it seems to me some of the people I know could play a funeral or parade and end up losing money, you know? I mean they could come out in the hole, huh? That would happen, huh?
